blocks.value: Position sizing means deciding how much money to invest in one stock or other investment. Choosing a good company is only part of the decision. The amount you put into it determines how strongly its performance can affect your overall portfolio. Even a strong business can become a risky holding if it takes up too much of your money.

Imagine This: A balanced meal contains different foods in suitable portions. Eating a very large quantity of only one food does not make the meal balanced. A portfolio also needs sensible portions: each investment should have a size that fits its role and the risk it brings.

Investors often set a maximum allocation for a single company, sector or investment idea. There is no one percentage that is right for everyone. The appropriate size depends on your total portfolio, financial goals, time horizon, confidence in your research and ability to handle a loss.

Suppose your portfolio is worth ₹5,00,000 and you decide to limit any one company to 10%. That means the maximum planned allocation is ₹50,000. If you invest ₹50,000 and that share falls by 20%, the holding loses ₹10,000. That is a 2% fall in the original ₹5,00,000 portfolio, assuming the other investments do not change.

This illustrates why position size matters. The same 20% share-price fall has a very different effect if the holding is ₹10,000 rather than ₹2,00,000. A large position can turn one company-specific problem into a major portfolio setback.

Position size should be considered alongside diversification. If you own several companies from the same industry, your total exposure to that industry may be much larger than any single-stock percentage suggests. Also remember that a holding can become oversized if its price rises substantially.
Think in both rupees and percentages. Before buying, calculate what the holding will represent in your portfolio and estimate how much a realistic fall could affect your overall finances.

A percentage limit is a planning tool, not a guarantee of safety. Never use money needed for essential expenses or near-term commitments simply because your chosen position limit leaves room for another purchase.

blocks.question: What does position sizing mean?
choices: Deciding how much to allocate to one investment

blocks.question: A ₹50,000 position in a ₹5,00,000 portfolio represents:
If that ₹50,000 holding falls 20%, what is its loss?
Why does position size matter?
choices: It affects how much one investment can influence the whole portfolio

blocks.question: What should influence the size of a position?
choices: Portfolio size, goals, risk capacity and concentration
